overview.description: Sjavs (pronounced 'Shows' or 'Shavs') is a popular card game in the Faroe Islands and parts of Denmark. It is a derivative of the German game Schafkopf, played with a stripped deck of 32 cards (standard Skat/Piquet deck). The game involves bidding, trump calling, and trick-taking, with a unique scoring system based on 'Rubbers' (first to reach 0 points from 24). It is highly strategic and social.

history.origins: Introduced to the Faroe Islands by Danish merchants or sailors familiar with German Schafkopf. The name 'Sjavs' likely comes from *Schafkopf*.
timeline: 1800s: Becomes the dominant game in TÃ³rshavn.
Present: Remains the most popular card game in the Faroes, often played in tournaments.
history.evolution: The rubber scoring system (subtracting points) is unique to Sjavs compared to modern Schafkopf.
history.cultural: Winning a rubber is cause for buying drinks. Being 'stuck' at 24 points is a humiliation.

setup.deck: 32 cards: the 2s through 6s are removed from a standard 52-card pack. Six cards are permanent highest trumps (Club Q, Spade Q, Club J, Spade J, Heart J, Diamond J); remaining cards rank A, K, Q, 10, 9, 8, 7. Point values: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2; 120 points in the pack.

rules.objective: Win tricks worth points. Reduce score from 24 to 0.
rules.gameplay: After the deal, dealer's left has first bid: each player states the length of their longest trump suit (five or more cards) or Pass; the longest length wins, and clubs beats another suit of the same length. The bid winner then announces trump. Dealer's left leads; play is clockwise. Players must follow suit when able and may trump or discard when void. The winner of each trick leads to the next. There are eight tricks; then each side counts card points in the tricks they won.
keyRules: Must follow suit if able; may trump or discard when void.
Six permanent trumps (Club Q, Spade Q, Club J, Spade J, Heart J, Diamond J) rank above trump-suit cards; then A, K, Q, 10, 9, 8, 7 in trump.
Bidding: state length of longest 5+ trump suit or Pass; longest wins; same length clubs beats. Bid winner names trump.
120 points per deal; rubber: count down from 24, first to 0 wins.

strategy.basic: Count trumps. There are 8 cards per suit. If you have 5 trumps, bid. If you have 4, check your partner via signaling. Lead Aces of non-trump suits early to cash them in before they get trumped.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Partner' Signal: Discard high-low to show strength. If your partner leads a suit you are void in, discard a 10 to give them points (Schummeln/Smearing).
strategy.advanced: Rubber Strategy: If you are at 2 points and opponents are at 20, prevent them from winning a 'Grand' or high-value game even if it costs you a simple game loss. Defensive bidding to block their strong suit is key.
tips: Clubs are often the best suit to name if lengths are equal.
Jacks are usually high trumps in Grand.

list.name: Three-player Sjavs
list.description: 10 cards each, 2 to table face down. Bidding same; one player makes trumps and plays alone vs the other two. Trump maker may discard one or two cards and pick up from table. Three columns on score sheet; soloist subtracts on win, opponents each subtract on loss.

list.name: Two-player Sjavs
list.description: Four face-down and four face-up cards per player in rows, plus 8 cards in hand. Face-up count as hand; when a table card is played the one under it is turned up. Bidding up to 12 possible.

difficulty.easy: Bids on short suits; wastes Aces; ignores partner.
difficulty.medium: Bids on 5+ trumps; smears points to partner.
difficulty.hard: Expert 'Bid-Optimizer'; calculates EV of bidding vs passing based on Rubber score; reads partner's signals perfectly.

phases.label: Deal
phases.notes: Deal 8 cards each: in fours if pack was cut, in eights if tapped.

phases.label: Bidding
phases.notes: Dealer's left first; state length of longest 5+ trump suit or Pass; longest wins, clubs beats same length. If no one has 5+, redeal.

phases.label: Announce Trump
phases.notes: Bid winner announces trump suit; must choose clubs if holding equal length in clubs and another suit.

phases.label: Play
phases.notes: Dealer's left leads; must follow suit; may trump or discard when void. Trick winner leads next. Eight tricks.
